title: Middle Score
statement: A judge panel always has an odd number of judges. To ignore unusually high or low scores, the final score is the one in the middle position once all scores are put in increasing order. Return that middle score.

answerKey.pattern: Sort a copy of the scores and return the item at index n / 2 (rounded down)
keyPoints: Sort the scores in increasing numeric order
With n odd, the middle index is Math.floor(n / 2) (n / 2 in Java integer division)
In JavaScript, pass a numeric comparator; the default sort compares as text
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(n) for a sorted copy, or O(1) extra when sorting in place
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Repeatedly removing the smallest and largest: O(n²)
Quickselect finds it in O(n) on average (not needed here)

hints: Where does the middle score sit once the scores are in order?
Sort, then pick the item in the middle position. With 5 scores that is index 2.
In JavaScript, [10, 9, 1].sort() gives [1, 10, 9]. Use sort((a, b) => a - b).
